info.title: MemberRegistrations API
info.description: Member registrations, ministries, event series, derived attendance, and shepherding. Attendance counts are computed from series schedules, imported occurrence lists and attendance registries; shepherding calls are append-only. Browser clients call /auth/* and /gateway/v1/*; the gateway holds the API bearer and derives X-Actor-Id from the officer session.

x-gateway.description: Browser traffic calls this prefix with an officer session; the gateway injects the API bearer and derived X-Actor-Id, then rewrites to /v1.

bearerAuth.description: Server-to-server API token. Never held by a browser.

EventScheduleGuard.description: Computed by the same function the write guard calls; read-only on the wire. `reasons` is empty when `locked` is false.

rrule.description: The RRULE body: DAILY with an optional INTERVAL 1-7 and no other key, WEEKLY with BYDAY and INTERVAL 1-4, MONTHLY with BYMONTHDAY, or MONTHLY positional with BYSETPOS=±1 and exactly one BYDAY. A weekly rule carrying INTERVAL is stored with WKST=SU.

day.description: A weekday inside each cycle, MON-SUN (never the rrule MO-SU); refused for a single-date period.

EventScheduleWrite.description: Exactly one arm: `{ recurrence: { rrule, endsOn? } }` for a recurring event, or `{ period: { frequency, day? } }` for a period event. The arm that does not match the event type is refused 422, and so is a body carrying both arms or neither.

schedule.description: Computed by the same function the write guard calls; read-only on the wire. `reasons` is empty when `locked` is false.
Computed by the same function the write guard calls; read-only on the wire. `reasons` is empty when `locked` is false.

dates.description: The event’s shape, derived from its own stored occurrences: `week` when its dates cluster inside one week (a seven-date period), `date` when they are a cycle apart (a single-date period). Null only when the event holds no occurrence at all, so there is no date to measure and no shape claim can be made.

definition.description: The period’s definition as it was written at save - a snapshot, never a live lookup, so a renamed definition never rewrites an event.

post.summary: USSD gateway entry (HMAC, not bearer)
post.description: The aggregator signs `timestamp + nonce + raw body` with USSD_GATEWAY_SECRET. A timestamp more than 300 seconds from now, a missing or invalid signature and a replayed nonce are 401; the phone is rate-limited per hash (10/min) and client address (30/min). The raw phone is never stored, returned or logged. USSD is disabled by configuration in production (503 ussd_disabled).

200.description: The whole screen for this frame, with Cache-Control: no-store.

401.description: The signature, timestamp or nonce is invalid.

422.description: Invalid request body or query parameters.

429.description: The phone hash or client address is over the rate limit.

post.summary: Nalo USSD entry (USERID auth, not bearer)
post.description: Nalo Solutions sends `USERID` (matched against USSD_NALO_USER_ID, no signature), `MSISDN`, `USERDATA`, `MSGTYPE` and `SESSIONID`. `SESSIONID` is stored as `external_id` under provider `nalo` so a continuation resolves the internal uuid; `USERDATA` over 64 characters is 422. The response omits `SESSIONID`, echoes `USERID`/`MSISDN`, truncates `MSG` to maxMsgChars with `…` only when needed, and sets `MSGTYPE` to `!done`. USSD is disabled by configuration (503 ussd_disabled).

200.description: The screen as Nalo wire, with Cache-Control: no-store; SESSIONID is omitted.

401.description: The USERID is absent or does not match USSD_NALO_USER_ID.

422.description: Invalid request body or query parameters.

post.summary: Start a member verification code
post.description: Resolves one destination from the member’s own contacts: the first unproven email, else the first unproven WhatsApp, else the first unproven phone (a proven contact is skipped, MR-24/AC-MR46). It generates one six-digit code and one single-use acceptance-page token, binds them to that contact and stores only their hashes plus a hash of the contact’s value (MR-26). The message carries the code and the link, for every channel. The response lists the masked destination and the expiry, never the code or the link. A member with no own email, WhatsApp or phone is 409 no_own_contact; a member whose every owned contact is proven, or who is officer-confirmed, is 409 already_verified; one send per 60 seconds and five per hour are 429 too_many_requests; a destination with no configured sender is 503 delivery_unavailable and nothing is stored.

202.description: The code was sent; the masked destination and the expiry, with Cache-Control: no-store.

404.description: The requested record was not found.

409.description: The member has no own email, WhatsApp or phone (no_own_contact), or every owned contact is proven or the member is officer-confirmed (already_verified).

429.description: The send throttle refused the request (too_many_requests).

503.description: A destination has no configured sender (delivery_unavailable).

delete.description: Withdraws every contact proof and the officer confirmation with an audit, and consumes any live code. It never removes a contact and never blocks an identified number (MR-31).

post.summary: Accept a verification code on the public member acceptance page
post.description: Unauthenticated by design: the single-use token and the six-digit code are the credential, whatever channel the code was sent to, and the answer carries only the masked destination. A wrong code is 400 code_invalid, an expired one 400 code_expired, the fifth wrong one 400 too_many_tries, and the per-token and per-address rate limit is 429 too_many_requests. The route answers no member data and the log carries no code, token or destination value (MR-51).

post.summary: Create the parent, with manual occurrences, one recurrence or one period
post.description: Creates the parent as a draft. Supply exactly one of manual `occurrences` (standalone), one `recurrence` (recurring) or a `period` - `{ id, cycleMonth }` for one cycle or `{ id, frequency: "monthly", day?, effectiveFrom? }` for a monthly rule the server resolves - never more than one; the range is derived from them and is not accepted, so `startDate`/`endDate` are read-only. A period resolves to ordinary occurrences in the same transaction and records its provenance (`period { id, name, cycle?, frequency?, day? }`); `effectiveFrom` anchors the 90-day window and is never stored, and a day on a single-date period is refused by name. `audienceIds` is the ordered applicability set (at least one, duplicates refused) and defaults to the seeded Everyone audience; `audienceId` remains a one-element alias for one round and, when both are sent, `audienceIds` wins and the alias must equal its first element. Composition is intersection: a member is in the event when they match every audience. `tracksMembers` defaults to true and `timezone` to UTC. `eventNo` is minted by the server and refused here by name (`422`); the retired `ministry` and `presbyterOnly` fields are likewise not part of the payload. 201 with Location naming the new detail URL.

post.summary: Generate missing occurrences for series and period events
post.description: Idempotent: an event already present for a series or period date is skipped and never overwritten, so a past date is never moved. Walks both kinds over the same `from..to` window - an rrule version, or a monthly period rule that keeps its parent’s times. Cancelled and extra exceptions are honoured for a series.

get.summary: List the named periods the event form can choose
get.description: The three declared periods - Communion Week, Gospel Week and Home Cells - as `{ id, name, definition, dates }`, served from the code catalogue. `dates` is the resolver’s `kind` projected onto the wire: `week` resolves to seven dates and may take a `day`; `date` resolves to one date and refuses it. A period resolves to UTC calendar dates and is stored as ordinary occurrences, so this is a read-only choice list, not a resource.

200.description: The three periods with their declared definitions.

items.name: Communion Week
items.definition: The week of the monthly communion service: week 1 of the cycle month, the seven days ending on that month’s first Sunday.

items.name: Gospel Week
items.definition: The last week of the month before, when ministries hold their meetings: the week before Communion Week.

items.name: Home Cells
items.definition: The Monday of week 1 of the cycle month - the Monday of Communion Week, one date.

post.summary: Resolve a recurrence or a named period to dates, without persisting
post.description: Resolves `recurrence` or a `period` - exactly one - to the dates the event would be created with. A period takes either create shape: `{ id, cycleMonth }` resolves one cycle once, and `{ id, frequency: "monthly", day?, effectiveFrom? }` walks the create’s 90-day window from `effectiveFrom` (default today, UTC), skipping dates that have passed. Nothing is written. `occurrences[].expected` is the intersection count for the supplied audience set at that date; `audienceCounts[]` carries each audience’s own count, which is a secondary label and does not sum to `expected`. An empty intersection is a real answer, not an error.

200.description: The resolved dates with their intersection and per-audience counts.

put.summary: Replace an event’s rule under the edit guard
put.description: The edit form’s save. The body takes exactly one arm - `{ recurrence: { rrule, endsOn? } }` for a recurring event, or `{ period: { frequency, day? } }` for a period event - and the arm must match the event’s type, which is fixed at create (`422` otherwise). `day` is `MON`-`SUN`, never the rrule’s `MO`-`SU`. The guard is enforced server-side: the parent read’s `schedule.locked` is computed by the same function this write calls, and a write while it is closed answers `409 recurrence_locked`. `effectiveFrom` is derived from the version in force, never sent. The write replaces the version in force with the same `effectiveFrom` (or the stored period fields) in one transaction, deletes only future `scheduled` rows - a future `cancelled` row survives, and exceptions re-apply on regeneration - then regenerates the event’s current window; it never extends the horizon, and `generated: false` says the window could not be produced. The answer carries the rule and provenance stored after the write, not an echo of the request.

post.summary: Publish the draft revision and materialise its instances
post.description: Requires an `active` event and a saved draft. `If-Match` pins a content token over slots, templates and flier (not the revision, because a draft edits in place). Materialises one instance per slot and occurrence over the 90-day horizon and applies the send-time policy to `delivery_at`. Refusals: `409 event_not_active`, `409 cadence_too_coarse` when a `starts` slot meets a trigger coarser than 15 minutes, `422 slot_in_past`, `422 duplicate_slot_time`, `422 template_required`, and `412 plan_content_stale` on a stale token. Republishing the published revision returns the same instances and creates none.

200.description: The published revision and its instances.

404.description: The requested record was not found.

409.description: The request conflicts with the current state.

412.description: The plan content has moved past the token in `If-Match`.

422.description: Invalid request body or query parameters.

post.summary: Cancel the published revision
post.description: Cancels the plan’s `scheduled` instances; created inbox messages and sent deliveries remain. A queued job drains as a no-op because the handler claims with a status re-check, and a cancelled instance does not block republishing the same moment.

200.description: The cancelled revision and how many instances stopped.

404.description: The requested record was not found.

409.description: The plan has no published revision (plan_not_published).

post.summary: Publish a one-off change notice
post.description: Writes its own `notification_change_notices` row and its own `change` instance to the published plan’s audience. It touches no slot and no future instance; the notice carries its own WhatsApp template and parameters and its own email subject and body because a published revision is frozen.

404.description: The requested record was not found.

409.description: The request conflicts with the current state.

422.description: Invalid request body or query parameters.

get.summary: Read the plan’s instances and their counts

200.description: Every instance for the plan, ordered by send instant.

404.description: The requested record was not found.

post.summary: Retry a failed delivery once (audited)
post.description: Accepts only a `failed` delivery (`409 delivery_not_failed` otherwise), re-renders from the revision the instance pinned, re-checks live mutes and blocks (so a retry may end `skipped`), and records `field = delivery_retry`, `source = admin` and the actor.

200.description: The delivery, now pending.

404.description: The requested record was not found.

409.description: The delivery is not failed (delivery_not_failed), or its failure is terminal (delivery_not_retryable) — a retry cannot fix a rejected destination or a missing provider.

post.summary: Replay one sent delivery as a new row (audited)
post.description: Writes a **new** delivery row that points at the original through `replayOf`, leaves the original untouched, and records the actor and the original id in `notification_delivery_events`. One delivery at a time, never for a list or a group: a bulk replay is how an officer duplicates a message to many members. Only an original with `replayOf` null is replayable, and each original at most once, so a second attempt is refused with `already_replayed` among the failed checks, and a failed replay is retried rather than replayed again. Every other delivery is refused `409 replay_not_valid` naming the failed checks unless each holds at the request: the instance and its event are not cancelled or archived; the message still exists and is not anonymised, or — for a guardian-routed delivery — the guardian route is still live; a live contact exists for the channel, or the guardian’s; no live mute covers that event or period and no live channel block applies; the cadence would not filter it; and the occurrence is today or later. A `change` notice is never replayed, and a `skipped` delivery stays refused until its reason is lifted through the preferences surface.

201.description: The new delivery row, pointing at the original.

replayed.summary: A replay of a sent SMS

404.description: The requested record was not found.

409.description: The original is not replayable (replay_not_valid, naming the failed checks — including already_replayed for an original already replayed once).

post.summary: Retry up to 100 failed deliveries by explicit id (audited)
post.description: The page’s “Retry all failed”, by the **explicit ids** the officer saw and never by a filter. Each id is re-checked against the live row — still `failed`, still `transport_unavailable` — and a row that is no longer failed, whose failure is terminal, or that no longer exists is reported **refused** rather than silently retried; the response names both counts and every id’s outcome. The actor is recorded per retried row in `notification_delivery_events`. One call carries at most 100 ids.

200.description: Both counts and the per-id outcome.

422.description: An invalid body, or more than 100 ids (batch_too_large).

put.description: One image of `image/webp`, `image/jpeg` or `image/png`, at most 2 MiB, sniffed by its magic bytes (a content type that disagrees with the bytes is refused). It is stored in the configured `FlierStore` (`db` in the register, or `s3` such as MinIO locally and R2 hosted) and the row records the store, the storage key, the media type, the size, the sha256 and a 32-byte token. Uploading on a published revision writes a new revision with a new token, so a sent URL keeps resolving to the image it was sent with.

200.description: The stored flier’s metadata and its public URL.

400.description: A valid request whose values cannot be used as asked.

404.description: The requested record was not found.

409.description: The request conflicts with the current state.

413.description: The flier exceeds the 2 MiB limit.

get.summary: Read the flier’s metadata
get.description: The type, size, hash, upload time and public URL; `404 flier_not_found` when the revision has none.

200.description: The stored flier’s metadata.

404.description: The requested record was not found.

delete.description: Removes the object and its row; removing one that is already absent is still 204.

404.description: The requested record was not found.

get.summary: The public flier image (no bearer)
get.description: Public by design and outside `/v1`: the 32-byte token is the whole credential and the URL is forwarded with every email and shown as the WhatsApp template’s header media. The app streams the object from the configured store, so no bucket is ever exposed directly. Immutable for a year, because a token names one object for ever.

200.description: The image bytes.

404.description: The requested record was not found.

get.summary: The four counts overall and per channel over a range
get.description: Computed **live** from `notification_deliveries` over `from`–`to` with no rollup table: `sent` is a delivery a provider accepted and carries no receipt claim, `failed` and `skipped` are their own statuses, and `queued` is `pending` or `sending`, so the four partition every delivery in the range. A skipped delivery is never counted as a failure — a mute is the member’s choice, not an outage. Dates are UTC calendar dates and default to the last seven days. The response carries `Cache-Control: no-store`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The range’s first UTC date; defaults to six days before `to`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The range’s last UTC date; defaults to today.

200.description: The overall counts and the same four per channel.

422.description: Invalid request body or query parameters.

get.summary: Cross-event deliveries, member and event joined
get.description: Every delivery across events, newest first, with the member named by **name and member number** beside the event, the channel, the status and the **masked** destination, so a failed row is traced to the person without exposing a contact value. `q` is a server-side join over the event name and the member number, never a client-side filter. Cursor-paged and `Cache-Control: no-store`.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: Only that delivery channel’s rows.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only that status’s rows.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Matches the event name or the member number, joined server-side rather than filtered in the client.

200.description: A page of deliveries with the member and event joined.

page.summary: One failed SMS with its member and event

422.description: Invalid request body or query parameters.

get.summary: Live mutes and channel blocks, named
get.description: FR-44’s one named exception: the Notifications page lists the live mutes and channel blocks with the member’s name and number, the kind, the scope or channel, the end date and how it was set (`ussd` or `admin`), because lifting one early means finding the person who asked. A row is live while it is neither revoked nor expired, and every row names its end date. No event surface lists members who declined, and this list is not reachable from one. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

parameters.name: live
parameters.description: `true` is the contracted value: the list holds rows that are neither revoked nor expired.

200.description: The live mutes and channel blocks.

live.summary: A muted event and a blocked channel

422.description: Invalid request body or query parameters.

post.summary: Send the failure digest on demand (audited)
post.description: Composes the **same digest the daily job sends** — each failed delivery since the previous digest, with its event, slot, channel, masked destination, attempts, sanitised error code and time — and emails it **once** to `failure_digest_to`, recording the actor so a manual send is not mistaken for the scheduled one. A second call while one is in flight does not send twice. A deployment with no recipient configured is refused and sends nothing.

200.description: The digest that was sent and how many failures it listed.

409.description: No failure-digest recipient is configured (`failure_digest_to` is unset), so nothing is sent (digest_unconfigured).

get.summary: Read the church notification defaults
get.description: The standard slot template a new plan copies, the church name, the email signature and reply-to, the SMS confirmation threshold, the approved WhatsApp template names and the send-time policy fields. A deployment with no stored row answers the built-in defaults rather than a 404.

200.description: The stored defaults, or the built-in ones when none is stored.

put.description: A partial write; every omitted field keeps its stored value. The standard slot template is validated against the same kind/anchor pairing a plan uses. The deployed trigger cadence is configuration, not a default, and is not writable here.

200.description: The defaults after the write.

422.description: Invalid request body or query parameters.
